title: Constant ring and module systems on the vertical sequence site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category of object universe $c$ and morphism universe $v$, with a Grothendieck topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $r$ be a coefficient universe such that $\mathcal C$ is essentially small in universe $\max(c,v,r)$. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with sections in this universe. On $\mathbf N\times\mathcal C$ use the vertical sequence topology $J_{\mathrm{seq}}$ [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] and the projection $p(n,U)=U$. Define the constant sequence ring $\Delta R=p^{-1}R$ by precomposition with $p^{\mathrm{op}}$: $(\Delta R)(n,U)=R(U)$, with the original vertical restrictions and identity horizontal maps. Define the constant module functor $\Delta_R:\operatorname{Mod}(J,R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(J_{\mathrm{seq}},\Delta R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], using the ordinary ringed-site module and coefficient conventions of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], by the same precomposition: $(\Delta_R M)(n,U)=M(U)$ with its original $R(U)$-action, original vertical restrictions, and identity horizontal maps; on a module morphism $f$, the component at $(n,U)$ is exactly $f_U$. The commutative-to-ring coefficient identification is the identity on sections. These are the existing quotientConstantRing and quotientConstant constructions, with no derived localization, flatness or K-flatness assumption and no invocation of the quotient-system flat-model comparison theorem.
